quests.none.headline: Choose a quest or an ask
quests.none.body: A quest is what one repository asks of another: held by the service, pulled by that repository's own agent, never written into its tree. Its page says where it stands and what ran it, with its acts at its head.
quests.gone.headline: This quest is no longer here
quests.gone.body: It was deleted, or it belongs to a workspace this window is not showing. Choose another in the list.
quests.card.lanesHint: It asks these lanes of {{repository}}: work for those lanes' sessions, not the whole repository.
quests.card.resumeTip: {{repository}} is held on this machine, so its quests wait. Resuming lets the driver start them; Repositories holds and resumes it too.
quests.card.waitsHint: Its taker asked another repository and is waiting for the answer. It resumes, in the same tree, once that quest is answered.
quests.empty.body: The family owes itself nothing right now. When a repository needs something from a sibling, it is asked for here — never edited across.
quests.detail.waitsWhy: It resumes, in the same tree, once this is answered.
quests.detail.answered: Answered — it resumes with what came back.
quests.detail.retried: #{{id}} will be tried again at the driver's next look. {{count}} more failed sessions park it again.
quests.detail.released: Released #{{id}} from your stop of {{session}}: the driver takes it up again at its next look.
quests.detail.declinePlaceholder: the reason — it is the part the asker can act on
quests.detail.deleteConfirm: This removes the quest from the ledger, and from every machine it reached once the delete syncs. It cannot be undone.
quests.detail.fileElsewhere: kept on the machine that published it
quests.detail.conflictsHint: Another machine's move reached the remote first. What this one attempted is kept here for a person; nothing was merged.
quests.compose.title: New quest
quests.compose.meta: published to the service; pulled by its owner
quests.compose.nobody.headline: Nobody can be asked yet
quests.compose.nobody.body: A quest goes from one registered repository to another, and none is registered yet. Repositories says how one joins.
quests.compose.hint: Say what is needed and why, with the evidence — never the change you would make; whoever works there may see a better answer.
quests.compose.titleLabel: What is wanted, in one line
quests.compose.caution: `{{repository}}` has not declared what it owns or accepts, so this may not be its problem. Worth checking before you rely on it.
quests.compose.filesLabel: files — kept on this machine and handed to whoever takes it here
quests.compose.stepHint: Published by the service when this closes done, on behalf of the same asker; a decline stops it. Write {parent} for this quest's id.
quests.compose.stepTitle: What is wanted next, in one line
quests.compose.stepBody: Why, and how to tell it is done
quests.session.title: Session
quests.session.hint: started by the driver, and observed rather than self-reported — the process runs on the driving machine; this is its record.
quests.session.stopped: session {{id}} is being stopped — the record will say the person ended it.
quests.session.orphanEnded: session {{id}} had nothing running it on this machine — its record now says so.
quests.session.notRunning: session {{id}} was not running here — its record says how it ended.
quests.session.runElsewhere: session {{id}} is run by another Daoris process on this machine, a terminal's — stop it there.
quests.detail.pausedOwn: You paused it on this machine: nothing of its work starts here until you resume it.
quests.detail.noDriver: Pausing and abandoning are a machine's driver's, so a browser offers neither: on the desktop, or at a terminal, `daoris-driver quest pause {{id}}` and `daoris-driver quest abandon {{id}}`.
